Sacramento: The FCE-Dillon system, which is being built for use as housing for elderly residents, is being equipped with an acoustical alarm system so that residents may summon help to their dwelling units as needed. The transmitter used for signalling is portable in nature (pencil-sized) and the resulting signal indicates to the resident manager where the call for help originates in the building.
B. Social Elements of the Program
i. Community Relations and Development
a) <u>Income Mix</u>: Studies have shown that economic differences frequently create barriers to lower income groups obtaining adequate housing. Design of the BREAKTHROUGH sites has taken this problem into consideration, and most of these sites will provide housing opportunities for a wide range of income levels, designed to make this housing attractive to the various target groups. The site financial programs have been established to permit this range in income levels.
b) Housing Type Mix: The different housing types developed within the program is noted earlier. In general, a range of types is offered on each site, consistent with the housing pattern in the local community and designed to provide the flexibility required to meet demands from varying income levels and family sizes.
c) <u>Community Facilities</u>: in order to encourage a sense of community and to provide necessary space for community activities, every site includes a community building with recreational and meeting space, including office space for the community organization.
d) <u>Community Organization</u>: The forms of community organization vary, with Homeowner's Associations being formed for those sites where home ownership is the primary form of marketing, Cooperatives on the two sites being marketed in this manner, and similar groups on the other ites. These are being structured through an arm of the site developer to be viable groups as the site becomes a part of the total community. Since every site includes common recreational and living space, a community organization is required to operate and maintain it, or to advise the sponsor/landlord who will carry this responsibility for those projects being marketed as rental units.
ii. Equal Opportunity
Moral, legislative and administrative considerations require that equal opportunity provisions be enforced in matters relating to training, employment, and housing. BREAKTHROUGH has provided a test bed for the development of guidelines in this area which will be further developed for other HUD program activities.
